about: NOTE-14 additions to notes_reader_ab_hard.json (same schema; category 'strictness'). Each strictness ask is expected as {'control': 'strictness', 'target': <a limit: global, min_edge, max_edge, near_wall, a quality measure, count; or a group: minimums, maximums, sizes, quality, angles, counts, all>, 'strictness': 'hard' | 'flexible'} beside the limits the same words set. The after-checks score them as mesh_requirements.check keeps them (the quote is the user's; a quote with a number names only the rows whose own words hold it). Look-alikes (a flexible hose, a hard anodised part) expect no strictness. r01-r03: size ranges for the whole mesh (min_edge and max_edge from one quote).

sentences.sentence: Min element length 5 mm. We're flexible around the minimum of 5mm, doesn't need to be a hard min.
sentences.reason: the founder's own wording: the 5 mm minimum is a target

sentences.sentence: Min. Element Length > 5 mm. It's okay to go below this in some places.
Shortest edge 2 mm, longest 8 mm, Jacobian above 0.6. The minimums are flexible.
sentences.reason: a group: the minimums are the shortest edge and the Jacobian floor, never the 8 mm maximum

sentences.sentence: Quad min angle 45, quad max angle 135, tria min angle 30. The angle limits are hard.
Global size 10 mm, warpage under 15, aspect ratio under 4. These are guidelines, not hard rules.
min 5 mm but flexible; max 15 mm is hard
sentences.reason: a mixed note: each limit by its own clause

sentences.sentence: No element under 0.5 mm, ever. That one is a hard limit.
Jacobian must stay above 0.5 at all costs.
Aim for roughly 3 mm elements where possible; the 1 mm minimum is strict.
We're flexable aroud the min of 5mm, dosent need to be a hard min
sentences.reason: typos: still flexible; the 5 mm minimum may be read as a size here or come from the saved standard

sentences.sentence: Rings round the bolt holes matter more than the 5 mm minimum - go below it where the washers need it.
Warpage < 15 (1% between 15 and 30 is acceptable) - the 30 is a hard stop.
sentences.reason: the allowance is already the limit's flexibility; the words make its outer value hard

sentences.sentence: Target about 4 million cells, max 6 million strictly.
sentences.reason: the target is a target anyway; the ceiling is said strict

sentences.sentence: Non-orthogonality under 65 if you can, but it isn't a hard limit.
The minimum element length is flexible. Actually no, keep it hard.
sentences.reason: a later sentence refines the earlier one; no number, so it is the minimum of the saved standard or of other notes

sentences.sentence: This is a flexible hose clamp bracket, 2 mm elements please.
sentences.reason: 'flexible' describes the part, not a limit

sentences.sentence: Hard anodised aluminium housing, mesh at 3 mm.
sentences.reason: 'hard' describes the finish, not a limit

sentences.sentence: Flexible duct, air at 5 m/s, prefer 8 prism layers.
sentences.reason: the duct is flexible; 'prefer' is about a layer count, which has no strictness of its own

sentences.sentence: element size 1-2 mm; 3 elements across every wall
sentences.reason: a range is the shortest and the longest edge, never one global size (read as global 2 mm on the live model, m483 round 11, 8c)

sentences.sentence: 2 to 5 mm elements please
keep the elements between 1 and 3 mm
aim for y+ around 1 on the walls
sentences.reason: soft words on a value: if a strictness entry comes back it must be on the y+ row itself (mesh_requirements.apply_strictness ties it by its quote), never an orphan told not applied
